source_title: UAV operation and prohibitions; critical-facility definitions
citation: Ohio Rev. Code §§ 4561.50-.51; incorporated definition at § 2911.21(F)(4)
uas_topic: Federal compliance; emergency-response interference; critical facilities
regulated_activity: Operating contrary to federal requirements; disrupting on-duty responders; photographing, recording, or loitering near a critical facility for specified criminal purposes
requirement_type: Prohibition with FAA-authorization exception for the federal-compliance provision
permit_or_approval_required: No separate state permit; an applicable FAA authorization supplies the stated exception to § 4561.51(A)
summary: Ohio Rev. Code § 4561.51 makes federally prohibited UAV operations a state offense unless the operator complies with an FAA authorization. It separately prohibits operations that disrupt, interrupt, or impair on-duty law-enforcement, fire, or emergency-medical personnel. Purposeful photography, recording, or loitering over or near a critical facility is prohibited when done to further a violent or threatening offense or to destroy or tamper with the facility. The incorporated facility definitions cover courts, police and correctional sites, military facilities, air-ambulance hospitals, commercial distribution centers, and a long list of fenced, posted, railroad, electronic, and industrial infrastructure. Penalties range from misdemeanors to a third-degree felony.
verification_status: Verified against current official code text, H.B. 77 history, and incorporated § 2911.21 definition
notes: The critical-facility provisions require a specified criminal purpose; they are not a categorical ban on ordinary commercial imaging near every listed facility. The emergency-response interference prohibition does not require that criminal purpose.

source_title: Unsafe operation of aircraft or UAV
uas_topic: Unsafe operation; endangerment; rights and safety
regulated_activity: Operating on land or water or in Ohio airspace in a manner that knowingly endangers a person or property or purposely disregards the rights or safety of another person
summary: Ohio Rev. Code § 4561.15(A)(5) prohibits operating an unmanned aerial vehicle on land or water or in the airspace over Ohio in a manner that knowingly endangers any person or property or purposely disregards the rights or safety of others. Under division (C), a violation may be punished by a fine of not more than $500, imprisonment for not more than six months, or both. The UAS provision was added by H.B. 77 and is distinct from the separate careless-or-reckless standard for manned aircraft in the section.
verification_status: Verified against current official code text and H.B. 77 history
notes: The statute does not define detailed operational thresholds for knowing endangerment or purposeful disregard; project facts and other applicable law remain important.

geographic_scope: Statewide boundary on specified local UAS regulation
source_title: Local use and operation of UAVs
uas_topic: Local authority; government fleets; recreational use on public property
regulated_party: Municipal corporations, townships, Chapter 1545 park districts, and counties
regulated_activity: Adopting ordinances, resolutions, or regulations concerning UAS
requirement_type: Affirmative but limited grant of local regulatory authority
summary: Subject to Ohio Rev. Code §§ 4561.50-.53, § 4561.52 authorizes a municipal corporation, township, Chapter 1545 park district, or county to regulate two categories: UAVs owned and operated by that governmental entity, and UAVs operated exclusively for hobby or recreational purposes in or above a park or other public property the entity owns. The section does not expressly label itself a preemption statute or independently authorize local regulation of ordinary commercial UAS operations. It nevertheless defines the UAS-specific local powers affirmatively granted by H.B. 77 and should be read with other generally applicable property and police powers.
verification_status: Verified against current official code text and authenticated official PDF
notes: Do not overstate this section as blanket preemption. It expressly grants two regulatory categories but does not state that all other local laws are void.

geographic_scope: All lands and waters administered by the Ohio Division of Parks and Watercraft
issuing_authority: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Parks and Watercraft
uas_topic: State parks; permission; recording; people, roads, boats, beaches; harassment
regulated_party: Any person operating or permitting operation of an unmanned aerial craft
regulated_activity: Operating within state-park boundaries or using the craft to record covered park activities, features, facilities, lands, or waters
requirement_type: Prohibition with chief or authorized-agent permission and designated-site exception
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — permission from the chief or authorized agent, unless using an airfield or landing zone maintained specifically for unmanned craft
summary: Ohio Admin. Code 1501:46-13-11 prohibits unmanned-aerial-craft operation within state-park boundaries without permission from the division chief or an authorized agent, except at an airfield or landing zone maintained for such craft. Separate permission is required to photograph, film, or record public activities, historical or cultural features, natural formations, division facilities, or other aspects of managed lands and waters. The rule also bars operation over open-air assemblies, beaches, boats, or roadways in division areas, requires FAA compliance, prohibits harassment of persons, and limits wildlife-harassment use to nuisance-control permittees who also have division permission.
verification_status: Verified against complete current official rule text
notes: The rule regulates operation within park boundaries, not merely launch and landing. Its recording restriction is broader than a conventional takeoff/landing property rule.

uas_topic: Nature preserves; natural areas; written permission; recording; harassment
regulated_activity: Launching, landing, or operating UAS over or within preserve or natural-area boundaries; recording covered features or activities
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — written permission from the division chief or authorized agent, requested at least 30 days in advance
summary: Ohio Admin. Code 1501:17-11-03 prohibits launching, landing, or otherwise operating an unmanned aerial craft in the airspace over or within a state nature preserve or natural area unless written permission is obtained from the division chief or an authorized agent. The request must be made at least 30 days in advance. The rule separately prohibits using unmanned craft to photograph, film, or record public activities, cultural or historical features, natural formations, division facilities, or other aspects of managed lands and waters without that permission, and strictly forbids using them to harass persons or wildlife.
verification_status: Verified against complete current official rule text
notes: Because the rule expressly reaches airspace over or within the boundaries, an off-property launch does not by itself avoid the state rule.

permit_or_approval_required: Yes — permission from the division chief or authorized agent
summary: Ohio Admin. Code 1501:3-2-16 provides that no person may operate, take off, or ascend within or from lands or waters administered by the Division of Forestry in an unmanned aerial vehicle or other listed aerial apparatus without permission from the division chief or an authorized agent. It separately bars voluntarily bringing, landing, or alighting an unmanned aerial vehicle within or on those lands or waters without the same permission. The rule does not publish a standard application, lead time, insurance threshold, or categorical commercial exception.
verification_status: Verified against complete current official rule text and 2026 review metadata
notes: Unlike the state-park and nature-preserve rules, this text is framed around operations on or from division lands and waters and does not expressly claim all overflight within the property boundary.

issuing_authority: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife
regulated_party: Hunters, drone operators, and persons aiding hunting
regulated_activity: Hunting, taking, or attempting to take wildlife with the aid or use of an aircraft or aerial drone
requirement_type: Prohibition with narrow post-take deer-recovery exception
commercial_operator_relevance: Low for ordinary AEC work; high if imagery or services are connected to hunting
summary: Ohio Admin. Code 1501:31-15-02(B) prohibits hunting, shooting, killing, taking, or attempting to take a wild bird or wild quadruped by means, aid, or use of an aircraft, expressly including aerial drones. A narrow exception allows a drone to aid recovery of a deer after the taking has occurred, provided no one involved in the recovery is employing a hunting device. If the deer is found alive, drone use must stop before hunting resumes; the operator may communicate the last location where the drone observed the deer.
verification_status: Verified against current official rule text effective July 6, 2026
notes: This rule is included because it expressly names aerial drones. It does not regulate unrelated mapping, inspection, or environmental work merely because it occurs during hunting season.

geographic_scope: Statewide; law-enforcement UAV surveillance and flights
source_title: Law-enforcement UAV surveillance, use, and data requirements
citation: Ohio Rev. Code §§ 4561.60-.64; H.B. 251, 136th General Assembly
uas_topic: Law enforcement; warrants; surveillance; lethal weapons; flight and surveillance data
regulated_party: Ohio law-enforcement agencies, peace officers, and persons flying on their behalf
regulated_activity: Law-enforcement surveillance flights, weaponization, private-person surveillance authorization, and data handling
requirement_type: Warrant and documentation requirements; enumerated exceptions; prohibitions
permit_or_approval_required: A judicial warrant is required when § 4561.61 applies; no separate operator permit is created
public_agency_only: Yes — applies to law-enforcement use and flights taken on behalf of an agency
commercial_operator_relevance: Moderate when a consultant flies on behalf of law enforcement
summary: Effective October 6, 2026, Ohio Rev. Code §§ 4561.60-.64 require a warrant when a peace officer uses UAS to enter or observe a house or place in circumstances where physical entry would require one, subject to enumerated warrantless uses such as exigencies, disasters, crash scenes, crime scenes, nonintrusive public observation, event threat assessment, and collaborative research or training. Agencies may not use lethal-weapon UAS or authorize surveillance by one private individual of another without specified consent. Agencies must document and verify flight data for each surveillance flight taken by or on their behalf, retain data relevant to proceedings, and generally treat flight and surveillance data as public records.
verification_status: Verified against official codified future-effective sections and H.B. 251 status
notes: This authority is enacted but not yet effective on the research date. The on-behalf-of documentation clause can reach contractor-operated surveillance flights for an agency.

issuing_authority: Ohio General Assembly / Ohio Secretary of State
source_title: Public-entity UAS foreign-adversary purchasing and operation restriction
citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 5501.84; H.B. 251, 136th General Assembly
uas_topic: Procurement; foreign adversaries; state funds; public-entity fleet operation
regulated_party: Ohio public entities and recipients using state funds in connection with covered purchases
regulated_activity: Purchasing, acquiring, funding, or operating UAS manufactured or assembled by a listed foreign adversary
requirement_type: Procurement, funding, and operation prohibition with federal-law exception
permit_or_approval_required: No permit; the statutory exception depends on federal law or regulation allowing continued purchase and operation
public_agency_only: Yes — principally governs public entities and state-funded acquisitions
commercial_operator_relevance: High for public-sector contracts and state-funded equipment
summary: Beginning October 6, 2030, Ohio Rev. Code § 5501.84 prohibits a public entity from purchasing or otherwise acquiring a UAS manufactured or assembled by a foreign adversary, prohibits use of state funds in connection with such systems purchased on or after that date—including through contracts, grants, and cooperative agreements—and prohibits public entities from operating such post-effective-date systems. A federal-law or federal-regulation allowance for continued purchase and operation supplies an exception. The Secretary of State must publish and update at least semiannually a registry derived from specified federal lists.
verification_status: Verified against official codified future-effective section, H.B. 251 status, and Secretary of State effective-date table
notes: The restriction is enacted but has a delayed effective date of October 6, 2030. It does not impose a present general ban on a private commercial fleet, but procurement and contract planning may need to anticipate it.

permit_or_approval_required: Yes — advance Department of Public Safety approval through the UAS request process; current flight-request guidance states at least 14 days in advance
summary: Ohio State treats all university property, including regional campuses and reasonable airspace above it, as a no-drone-fly zone unless the remote pilot first receives university approval and complies with imposed conditions. The process includes a UAS request form and operations agreement, with review by Public Safety and potentially communications, export-control, venue, and other offices. Current flight-request guidance calls for submission at least 14 days before the event, prohibits flight over people, and adds venue-specific controls. The policy also governs university-sponsored activities off property and requires accident and adverse-event reporting.

summary: Ohio Admin. Code 3341-6-50 applies to any person operating a UAS on or above Bowling Green State University property and to contracted vendors or university-funded UAS services. Private and hobbyist operations are prohibited. Commercial and governmental operations on or above university property, or elsewhere on behalf of BGSU, require advance Office of Risk Management approval to address compliance and insurance. geographic_scope: Kent State University-owned or leased property
source_title: Administrative policy regarding unmanned aircraft systems
uas_topic: No-fly zone; commercial operators; standoff distances; continuous operations
regulated_party: Employees, students, contractors, vendors, and third parties
regulated_activity: UAS flight operations on or above university property
requirement_type: No-fly rule with flight or continuous-flight approval
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — UAS Review Committee approval; request due at least two weeks before a flight or first continuous-operation flight
summary: Kent State is a no-drone-fly zone under Ohio Admin. Code 3342-5-12.16. All operations, including commercial contractor flights, require UAS Review Committee approval through a request submitted at least two weeks in advance. A continuous-operation approval may cover multiple flights for up to six months. Approved operators must stay in designated areas, avoid the Kent State airport, minimize ground and aviation risks, and ordinarily remain at least 50 feet from walkways, 200 feet from buildings, and 100 feet from parking lots or roads. Privacy, sensitive-data, marks, notification, and incident-reporting restrictions also apply.
verification_status: Verified against complete current official rule text
notes: The stated standoff distances could make many building-inspection or campus-mapping missions infeasible unless the committee modifies the approved operating area or conditions.

regulated_activity: Commercial or other business-purpose UAS operations and aerial recording on university property
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — written permission from the Director of Environmental Health and Safety Offices for business use; nonemployee private operators also need a written agreement
summary: Ohio Admin. Code 3339-16-17 requires a person conducting compensated, hired, or other business-purpose UAS work on Miami University property to submit mission, pilot, aircraft, and imaging information; provide a current remote-pilot certificate or COA; and obtain written permission from the Director of Environmental Health and Safety Offices. A nonstudent or nonemployee private operator must also enter a written agreement containing hold-harmless and indemnity terms and maintain at least $1 million in liability coverage naming Miami as an additional insured. issuing_authority: University of Cincinnati, Enterprise Risk Management / Public Safety

regulated_activity: UAS or model-aircraft operation on or above university property
requirement_type: Prohibition with institutional-purpose and authorization exceptions
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — University of Cincinnati authorization under its UAS-operation guidelines
summary: University of Cincinnati Policy 6.3.2 strictly prohibits UAS use on university property unless the flight is solely for research, education, or university operations; the university has authorized it; all external approvals have been obtained; and the mission avoids monitoring locations where people have a reasonable expectation of privacy. Recreational and personal-imaging flights are prohibited. The policy applies to third parties and contractors as well as university personnel, makes operators responsible for fines or damages, and permits law enforcement to ground noncompliant or dangerous operations. The university maintains a current online drone-flight approval request process.
